Estimate scale reliability from item responses

Source: R/psychometrics.R
sframe_reliability_results.Rd

Produces Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega for each scale defined in the instrument, along with the number of items and sample size.

Usage

sframe_reliability_results(
  data,
  instrument,
  scales = NULL,
  alpha = TRUE,
  omega = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A tibble or data.frame of responses. Item columns must be present.

instrument

An sframe object.

scales

Character vector or NULL. A subset of scale IDs to analyse. When NULL (default), all scales in the instrument are included.

alpha

Logical. Whether to compute Cronbach's alpha. Defaults to TRUE.

omega

Logical. Whether to compute McDonald's omega. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

An object of class sframe_reliability_report, a list with one element per scale. Each element holds scale_id, label, n_items, n, alpha, alpha_ci (Feldt's 95% confidence interval, as lower and upper), alpha_std and alpha_if_deleted, and with omega = TRUE, omega_t, McDonald's omega total from a 1-factor model. Every display reports alpha and omega_t. omega_h is kept for code that reads it: in a 1-factor model there are no group factors, so it carries no hierarchical meaning and can come out a rounding step above omega_t.

See also

sframe_scale(), sframe_item_results()

Other Analyse functions: run_analysis_plan(), score_scales(), sframe_assumption_results(), sframe_descriptives_results(), sframe_efa_readiness_results(), sframe_efa_solution(), sframe_item_results(), sframe_posthoc_results(), sframe_validity_results()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE)) {
  demo <- sframe_demo("likert_scale")
  rr <- sframe_reliability_results(demo$responses, demo$instrument, omega = FALSE)
  print(rr)
}
# }
